PHASE 4 ADDITION (2026-08-31): six new '<mode>_p4' sections carry the Tier-2 scenario-matrix dataset's per-output evidence. They are a SEPARATE namespace on purpose: the committed Phase 2 manifests cite their mode's key set verbatim, so adding a key to a bare '<mode>' section would silently redefine an already-accepted manifest. Phase 4 manifests carry a 'dataset': 'phase4' field and cite only '<mode>_p4' keys; a manifest with no 'dataset' field is a Phase 2 manifest (see tests/cpp_parity_live/_golden_manifest.py's DEFAULT_DATASET and tests/cpp_parity_live/_phase4_contract.py). Statuses used by Phase 4 and their meanings: 'verified' (every scenario on this route agreed, with the measured maximum difference recorded in the justification); 'known_divergent_scenario_scoped' (some scenarios agreed and some reproduce a named finding, with BOTH the agreeing maximum and the smallest divergence recorded so it is provable the tolerance absorbs no divergence); 'known_divergent_strict_xfail' (every scenario diverges); 'oracle_unavailable' (the harness cannot produce a valid oracle for this route at all - see F-45); 'python_side_unreachable' (the Python function cannot be called - see F-19); 'unverified' (no comparison was performed, so no tolerance is assigned). Three independent divergences identified in the Gate 0 crosswalk: (a) C++ zeroes a tree's contribution when f_Hgt<=0 OR f_Dia<=0; Python excludes only dbh<=0/NaN and still credits crown area to a zero/negative-height tree; (b) Python's species-to-equation mapping depends on a caller-supplied tree_code_dict — with the default None, every tree is assigned equation 39 ('Other'), which does not match C++'s per-species FVS index lookup; (c) Python assumes one tree per acre per record while C++ callers supply an explicit per-acre count. None of these are numeric-tolerance-bridgeable; each requires a Python-side fix or an explicit input-contract change before any atol/rtol is meaningful.

calc_canopy_cover vs the manifested canopy_cover golden, with the per-species crown-width equation supplied explicitly from the tracked FOF_SPP.CSV. 12 of the 14 successful per-tree scenarios agree and 4 of the 5 emitted stand aggregates agree: measured maximum relative difference 1.02e-06 and maximum |diff| 8.32e-04 ft2. The rtol 2e-06 is evidence-based, not tuned: C++ SMT_CalcCrnCov uses the literal 3.14159 (fof_mrt.cpp:1634) where Python uses numpy.pi, a fixed relative difference of 8.4e-07 in an expression linear in that constant, plus the C++ side's float32 arithmetic. The atol 1e-04 is the golden's own output resolution (crown areas and percentages are written through fmt(v, 4)). The 2 diverging trees and 1 diverging stand are strict xfails under F-02: C++ returns 0 crown area as soon as f_Hgt <= 0, while Python excludes a tree only for dbh <= 0, so it credits a zero- or negative-height tree 30.229674 ft2. Python's DEFAULT species mapping (equation 39 for every species) is a separate, larger divergence characterised separately and never relied upon: measured 40 % to 70 % relative error against the real per-species equations.
